articles.title: Two Boys Seriously Injured in E-Bike Crash on Windermere Road, Middleton
articles.excerpt: A serious collision involving an e-bike and a car on Windermere Road in Middleton has left two boys, aged 13 and 14, with serious injuries. The driver has been arrested as investigations continue.
articles.content_html:
Two boys were seriously injured following a collision between an e-bike and a car in Middleton on Monday evening, September 28. The incident occurred on Windermere Road at the junction with Wood Street around 8pm, prompting a major emergency response from police and paramedics.

Emergency services arrived quickly at the scene, where a large number of police and ambulance vehicles were deployed. A cordon was established across a stretch of the road as crews worked to assist the injured and investigate the circumstances of the crash. The two boys, aged 13 and 14, were taken to hospital for treatment of their serious injuries, according to a spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police (GMP).

The driver of the car, a man in his 20s, was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by driving without due care and attention. He has since been taken into custody for questioning. The road remained closed for several hours as officers from GMP's Serious Collision Investigation Unit conducted their inquiries, with evidence markers visible within the cordon.

GMP is appealing for information regarding the incident and is particularly interested in speaking to any witnesses or individuals who may have footage of the crash. Anyone with information is urged to contact police on 101, quoting log 3478 of September 28, or to reach out via the LiveChat function on the GMP website. Alternatively, reports can be made anonymously to Crimestoppers at 0800 555 111.

articles.title: Medequip to Manage Community Equipment Loan Service for Oldham, Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside
articles.excerpt: Medequip has been awarded a contract to provide the Community Equipment Loan Service for Rochdale, Oldham, Stockport, and Tameside, commencing on 1 October 2026.
articles.content_html:
Community equipment services provider Medequip has been awarded the contract to deliver the Community Equipment Loan Service (CELS) for Rochdale, Oldham, Stockport, and Tameside. This contract, awarded by a partnership of the four local authorities and the NHS Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board (ICB), is set to commence on 1 October 2026 and will initially run for three years, with an option to extend for an additional two years.

The CELS plays a crucial role in supporting both adults and children to live independently and safely at home. Medequip will manage the full lifecycle of community equipment, which includes procurement, delivery, installation, maintenance, repair, collection, decontamination, refurbishment, and recycling. This service is integral to the health and social care systems, facilitating timely hospital discharges and supporting reablement and recovery efforts.

To ensure continuity of service, Medequip will initially operate from the existing service depot in Dukinfield. Following this, the company plans to relocate to a new, purpose-built service centre within the Hollinwood Junction development. This modern facility, spanning 32,450 square feet, has been designed with sustainability in mind and will enhance operational capacity while supporting efficient service delivery across the four boroughs.

The new service centre will not only improve Medequip's ability to provide high-quality services but will also focus on maximising the collection, refurbishment, and reuse of equipment, aligning with sustainable circular economy principles. This development is expected to have a positive impact on local residents by ensuring they have access to necessary equipment that supports their independence.

articles.title: High Court Trial Begins Over Ownership of Hopwood Hall
articles.excerpt: A two-day trial in the High Court will determine the future of Hopwood Hall as Hopwood DePree seeks to reclaim his ancestral home from Rochdale Council.
articles.content_html:
A trial concerning the ownership of Hopwood Hall commenced today in the High Court in Manchester, with Hopwood DePree contesting Rochdale Council's control of the historic manor house. DePree, a descendant of the Hopwood family who constructed the hall in the 1420s, argues that the council has reneged on an agreement allowing him to purchase the property after he spent seven years collaborating with them on necessary repairs.

The Hopwood family owned the hall and its surrounding land, now home to Hopwood Hall College, until 1922. Following its sale in 1942, the hall was occupied by various temporary residents, including the de la Salle Brothers, who operated it as a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s. The building has since fallen into disrepair and was acquired by Rochdale Council, which still owns the Grade II-listed site.

DePree's legal action follows the council's decision in November 2024 to terminate an exclusivity agreement with him, stating that no commercially viable business model had been presented. He contends that the council must proceed with the ownership transfer, as the conditions of their agreement were met upon the granting of planning permission in 2022.

The outcome of this trial could significantly impact the future of Hopwood Hall, which has historical importance and potential for restoration. The court's decision will clarify whether DePree can reclaim his ancestral home or if the council will retain ownership and explore alternative plans for the property.

articles.title: Zambrero Opens New Mexican Restaurant on Mellor Street, Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Zambrero has launched its latest restaurant on Mellor Street, offering a menu of Mexican-inspired dishes and a commitment to donate meals to those in need.
articles.content_html:
A new Mexican restaurant, Zambrero, has opened its doors on Mellor Street in Rochdale. The restaurant launched at 11am on September 25, offering a diverse menu featuring burritos, bowls, tacos, nachos, and quesadillas, all made to order with fresh ingredients.

Zambrero is notable for its Plate 4 Plate programme, which donates a meal to someone in need for every burrito or bowl sold. Damian Bennett, development agent for Greater Manchester and West Yorkshire, expressed excitement about bringing fresh Mexican flavours to the area, stating, "We’re thrilled to bring fresh, feel-good Mexican flavours to Rochdale. There is something here for every taste with a fully customisable menu."

The menu caters to various dietary preferences, including vegetarian, vegan, and halal options, ensuring that all diners can enjoy the offerings. Zambrero aims to provide not only delicious food but also a way for customers to contribute to tackling world hunger with each meal purchased.

The opening of Zambrero is expected to enhance the local dining scene, providing residents with more options for casual dining while supporting a charitable cause. Customers can visit the restaurant to experience the new flavours and contribute to the Plate 4 Plate initiative.

articles.title: Man Charged with Manslaughter Following Death in Rochdale Town Centre
articles.excerpt: A 37-year-old man has been charged with manslaughter after a 52-year-old man died following an incident on South Parade in Rochdale. The victim was found unconscious on September 26.
articles.content_html:

A 37-year-old man has been charged with manslaughter after a 52-year-old man died following an incident on South Parade in Rochdale. The victim was found unconscious on September 26.

A 37-year-old man has been charged with manslaughter following the death of a 52-year-old man in Rochdale town centre. The victim was discovered unconscious on South Parade at approximately 1.30am on Saturday, September 26, and was taken to hospital but died later that day despite the efforts of emergency services.

Greater Manchester Police launched a murder investigation after the incident. In an update on Tuesday, September 29, a police spokesperson confirmed that Dougie Waring, of Marigold Street, Rochdale, has been charged and is scheduled to appear at Manchester and Salford Magistrates' Court today. Another man who was arrested in connection with the investigation has been bailed pending further inquiries.

Detective Chief Inspector Claire Brennan from GMP's Major Incident Team stated that a dedicated team of detectives is working to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incident. The police are continuing their investigation into the events leading up to the man's death.

This incident has raised concerns within the local community, and residents may be seeking further information regarding safety measures in the area. Anyone with information related to the case is encouraged to contact Greater Manchester Police.

articles.title: Why Rochdale says “cruckle”
articles.excerpt: A short guide to the local verb “cruckle”: what it means, where it comes from, and why people in Rochdale still call that awkward ankle‑twist by its own name.
articles.summary: A short guide to the local verb “cruckle”: what it means, where it comes from, and why people in Rochdale still call that awkward ankle‑twist by its own name.
articles.body:
If you grew up in parts of Rochdale you will probably recognise the line: “I cruckled my ankle.” Locally, to “cruckle” means to roll or twist an ankle — the small, nasty half‑twist you can often walk off but that still makes you wince. That is the everyday sense people in the borough use now, and it is the reason the word still turns up in conversation, social media and local memory.

How old is the word? It is not a modern invention. Historical dialect lexicons record a family of related words — crookle, crug, cruggle and similar forms — with meanings in the same semantic field (to bend, make crooked, crouch, hobble). These entries show the shape of an older northern and Scots dialect pattern in which a crook/krug root combines with a frequentative or verbalising ending (‑le) to make verbs that suggest bending or awkward movement. The Dictionary of the Scots Language lists cruggle/cruckle/krukel and cites quotations from the late 19th and early 20th centuries showing meanings such as “to crouch” or “to huddle.”

Is “cruckle” uniquely Rochdale? That depends on how you measure uniqueness. On the one hand, historical records show related forms elsewhere in northern England and in Scots dialects: the root and word‑building pattern are regional rather than invented in a single street. On the other hand, folk‑linguistic evidence — what people themselves say about local speech — ties the word strongly to Rochdale today. A recent perceptual‑dialect study of Greater Manchester (published 2024) collected hundreds of crowd‑sourced “draw‑a‑map” responses and keyword comments; among the words respondents associated with Rochdale was “cruckle,” listed alongside other locally salient items such as “guinnel” (ginnel). That kind of data shows a living social association: speakers and listeners link the term particularly with Rochdale speech.

Why does that combination (regional history + local claim) happen? Dialect words survive or disappear for lots of reasons — local mobility, schooling, media influence, and family speech habits all matter — but certain small words endure because they carry social meaning. A term like cruckle does two jobs at once: it names a familiar action, and it signals belonging. Perceptual dialect research treats items like this as useful indicators of both language change (who still uses the word) and language attitude (which words people believe mark their place).

What can dialect research tell us beyond smells of nostalgia? Two lessons stand out. First, forms such as cruckle fit predictable historical patterns (crook/krug + ‑le) that linguists have documented across northern English and Scots; that explains why related words appear in different places and times. Second, modern mapping and keyword studies show that local recognition — not just historical presence — determines whether words feel “from” a place. In Rochdale’s case, continued local use and local identification appear to have made cruckle feel distinctly Rochdale even while similar forms exist elsewhere.

A final practical note: it is difficult to prove absolute exclusivity for any dialect word. Administrative borders do not stop words from spreading, and historical records sometimes show wider distribution than folk memory suggests. What we can say, on the basis of published dialect lexicons and a 2024 perceptual study, is this: cruckle has roots in older northern dialect vocabulary, and today it is strongly associated with Rochdale in people’s perceptions and daily talk. If you have family spellings, old letters or recorded uses of the word, local archives and dialect projects welcome contributions — small words like this are precisely the material researchers need to trace how language and place stay entwined.

A High Court hearing is scheduled for tomorrow, September 29, concerning a dispute between Hollywood actor Hopwood DePree and Rochdale Council regarding the future of the historic Hopwood Hall in Middleton. The case arises after the council terminated its exclusivity agreement with DePree at the end of 2024, which had allowed him to lead the redevelopment of the Grade II*-listed site.

DePree, who has claimed to have invested over £750,000 in the restoration of Hopwood Hall, argues that he has a legally binding agreement to purchase the property. The council, however, contends that the agreement was ended due to insufficient progress on the project and the need to explore other investment opportunities. Following the termination, the site was closed to volunteers due to alleged health and safety breaches, according to the council.

The upcoming trial at the Manchester Civil Justice Centre will determine whether the council is obligated to transfer ownership of Hopwood Hall to DePree. His Honour Judge Hodge KC will preside over the two-day proceedings, during which both parties will present their arguments.

The outcome of this case could significantly impact the future of Hopwood Hall, a site with historical significance dating back to the 1400s. DePree has expressed hope that the court will rule in his favour, allowing him to continue his efforts to restore the building.

articles.title: Not Quite Big Band to Perform at Rochdale Town Hall on 7 November
articles.excerpt: The 17-piece Not Quite Big Band will headline a show at Rochdale Town Hall, featuring music from Sinatra to Avicii, on Saturday 7 November.
articles.content_html:
Greater Manchester’s 17-piece Not Quite Big Band is set to perform a headline show at Rochdale Town Hall on Saturday 7 November. The band will present two live sets, showcasing a diverse range of music from classic artists like Frank Sinatra to contemporary hits by Avicii.

The event will feature round-table seating, a bar, and space for dancing, creating an engaging atmosphere for attendees. The band has gained significant popularity, amassing over 10 million views online, and previously held a two-year residency at Manchester’s Hotel Gotham, in addition to performances on the Isle of Man.

This upcoming show marks a return to the round-table format that the band used during its residency, promising a unique experience for local audiences. Tickets for the event are available through Ticket Tailor, allowing fans to secure their place for an evening of lively entertainment.

As the date approaches, local residents are encouraged to attend this exciting event, which not only highlights the talents of the band but also supports community engagement at Rochdale Town Hall.

articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks will commence on multiple roads from 12 October 2026, lasting until 8 November 2026, with work taking place overnight.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks will begin on various roads in Rochdale from 12 October 2026, continuing until 8 November 2026. The work will take place overnight, from 8pm to 5am each night, to minimise disruption during peak hours.

The roadworks will be carried out in three phases, with only one phase active at a time. Alternative routes for vehicles will be clearly signed on site as necessary to guide motorists around the affected areas.

Residents and commuters are advised to plan their journeys accordingly during this period. The council has provided a map of roadworks across Greater Manchester, which can be viewed for further details on restrictions and diversions.

For more information, visit the Rochdale Borough Council website or consult local traffic updates as the start date approaches.

articles.excerpt: Hopwood Hall College has launched new student uniforms supplied by Rochdale-based ICON Sports, enhancing the academic experience for students across its campuses this academic year.
articles.content_html:
Hopwood Hall College has introduced new student uniforms for the academic year, supplied by Rochdale-based company ICON Sports. The new uniforms are being worn by students across both of the college's campuses, and some tutors have also received branded workwear as part of the initiative.

The decision to partner with ICON Sports followed a procurement and evaluation process, with the college highlighting the local business's base in Rochdale as a significant factor in their selection. ICON Sports is known for producing custom sportswear and workwear, aligning with the college's vocational focus.

Julia Heap OBE, Principal and CEO of Hopwood Hall College, expressed enthusiasm about the new uniforms, stating, "The new term has started with a bang and there’s a great energy across our campuses – partly because of the new uniforms!" She added that the students have quickly embraced the new kit, which is designed to support their success in gaining vocational qualifications, including T Levels.

This partnership not only enhances the student experience but also supports the local economy by investing in a growing Rochdale business. The college aims to continue fostering such collaborations that benefit both students and the community.

articles.title: Rochdale Council Launches Increased Parking Patrols Outside Schools
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has launched a new campaign to improve safety for schoolchildren by increasing parking enforcement outside schools and reminding drivers to stop for crossing patrols.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has initiated a new campaign titled “Stop Means Stop” aimed at enhancing safety for schoolchildren by reminding drivers of their responsibilities at school crossing patrols. The campaign was launched by Councillor Dylan Williams, the council’s cabinet member for Highways and Facilities, at St Luke’s Primary School in Heywood.

As part of the campaign, the council announced that parking enforcement patrols outside schools will be increased. This decision follows the recording of 137 instances over the past five years where drivers failed to stop for school crossing patrols, including cases where patrols had already stepped into the road. Councillor Williams highlighted the dangers posed to children, stating, “This is obviously a real danger for schoolchildren across the borough. It’s really important that people stop.”

In addition to the increased patrols, the council is urging drivers to keep yellow lines and school keep-clear markings free of parked vehicles. A crossing patrol worker at St Luke’s, identified as Chris, noted that vehicles parked on zigzag lines obstructed both his view and the view of passing drivers, which could lead to dangerous situations.

The increased parking patrols will not follow a fixed schedule, allowing for flexibility in enforcement. A parent at St Luke’s Primary School suggested that families should consider parking further away to leave space clear near the crossing, contributing to a safer environment for children. The council’s efforts aim to foster a safer atmosphere for schoolchildren as they arrive and depart from school.

articles.title: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Approves Mayoral Development Corporation for Rochdale
articles.excerpt: The Greater Manchester Combined Authority has approved a Mayoral Development Corporation for Rochdale, aimed at enhancing regeneration efforts in the area.
articles.content_html:
The Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) has approved the establishment of a Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) for Rochdale, alongside similar initiatives for Oldham, Bolton, and Tameside. This decision, made on Friday, is part of a broader strategy to stimulate regeneration across the northern regions of Greater Manchester.

The Rochdale MDC will focus on revitalising key areas within the borough, with plans to deliver 2,000 new homes and community facilities across six sites. The initiative is expected to attract investment and improve local infrastructure, although specific project details are still to be confirmed.

This approval follows the successful implementation of a similar MDC in Stockport, which has been credited with driving significant development in that area. The GMCA aims to replicate this success in Rochdale and the other boroughs involved, fostering economic growth and community enhancement.

Next steps will involve detailed planning and consultation with local stakeholders to ensure that the development meets the needs of residents and businesses in Rochdale. The GMCA's commitment to these projects signals a proactive approach to addressing local challenges and promoting sustainable development in the region.

articles.title: Councillor Calls for Urgent Meeting Over Disorder Reports in Middleton Town Centre
articles.excerpt: Councillor Lee Wolf has requested an urgent meeting with police and council officers following reports of disorder in Middleton town centre and at the former Durnford Street School site, urging immediate action to address the situation.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Live updates, newest first.

20:57, 28 September 2026

Councillor Lee Wolf has requested an urgent meeting with police and council officers following reports of disorder in Middleton town centre and at the former Durnford Street School site, urging immediate action to ensure community safety.

Councillor Lee Wolf has called for an urgent meeting with Greater Manchester Police and council officers in response to increasing reports of disorder in Middleton town centre and at the former Durnford Street School site. In a post on a local Facebook group, he expressed concern that the area could become a 'no-go zone' for residents if immediate action is not taken.

Councillor Wolf highlighted that groups of young people have been entering the former school site daily, climbing onto its roof and throwing stones and mud at passing and parked vehicles. He noted that some parents have even dropped their children off at the site, which he described as inadequately secured. He is advocating for the installation of surveillance cameras at the location, including those capable of capturing vehicle registration plates.

In his post, Councillor Wolf urged residents to report every incident to the police to ensure there is an official record of the disturbances. Local residents have echoed his concerns, with reports of dangerous behaviour including a cyclist in a balaclava nearly colliding with a pedestrian and fireworks being directed towards shops and cars. Other incidents included fireworks being set off in bins outside businesses, and young people reportedly throwing fireworks and entering food shops near Tesco.

The councillor's call for action comes amid growing unease in the community regarding safety in the town centre. The meeting he has requested aims to address these issues directly with police and council officials, seeking a coordinated response to restore safety and security for residents.
